rules: Import the pattern's prelude in a routes file (`ruststream_zeromq::queue::prelude::*`, `fanout::prelude::*` or `rpc::prelude::*`) for its policy as `Publish`, and `ruststream_zeromq::prelude::*` to mount several patterns (Prelude page).
Pick the broker by shape (Broker page): `ZmqQueue` (PUSH/PULL) for competing consumers, `ZmqFanout` (PUB/SUB) for broadcast filtered by name prefix, `ZmqRpc` (DEALER/ROUTER) for request and reply.
Declare a subscription by its name, `#[subscriber("jobs")]`, which is frame 0 of every message, and set `read_ahead` on the broker (Subscriptions page).

State the side on the endpoint with `ZmqEndpoint::bind(addr)` or `ZmqEndpoint::connect(addr)` on `tcp://` or `ipc://`, and write it as a type, `ZmqQueue<Connect>`, only where a mount site names one (ZmqEndpoint page).

Bound a handler's injected publisher with a core capability such as `Out<impl Publisher, Slot>` and import `ruststream::prelude::*` alone in a handler body, since a ZeroMQ send takes the frames alone (Publishing page).
Retry with `retry_after` and cap with `.max_attempts(n)` at the mount site: `ack` reports `AckError::Unsupported`, and the framework publishes and counts every copy (Retries page).

Bind the retry publisher with `.out_retry(Publish)` on a `ZmqQueue` or `ZmqFanout` this service binds, and with `.out_retry(token).to("name")` on one it dials and on every `ZmqRpc` responder (out_retry page).
Park spent deliveries with `.dead_letter(name)` through a retry publisher on another endpoint, because a name on the subscription's own endpoint comes back to it (Dead letters page).

Send a `ZmqQueue` worker's replies through a queue on an endpoint of its own with `bindable()`, `.bind(Publish)` and `.out_reply(token)`, because the bound queue's publisher refuses any other name (Replies page).
Answer on `ZmqRpc` with a reply handler whose type names no destination, a `reply("..")` fallback, and a transform of your own declaring `Destination = Names` that reads `reply-to` (Responders page).
Ask a `ZmqRpc` service from a handler bounded `Out<impl RequestReply>`, and give up through the request's timeout rather than a `select!` arm (Request-reply page).
Batch a `ZmqQueue` or `ZmqFanout` subscription with `.batch(n)`, which closes a batch at `n` deliveries or 20 ms after its first, and answer `ZmqRpc` requests one at a time (Batches page).

Test by handing the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start` with the `testing` feature in dev-dependencies, address a broker as `tb.broker::<ZmqQueue>()`, and run the same body over sockets with `TestApp::start_live` (Testing page).
